key_insight: Soft information turns small-margin reads into erasures, and latch resolution time supplies it almost free. Charge-transfer sensing and offset cancellation carry most of any 5x Cs cut.
killer_doubt: Gaussian tails: raw BER 1e-4 to 1e-3 buys only 1.2x Cs (3.72 to 3.09 sigma). A 1 fF cell gives 14 mV on 35 fF; on-die LDPC adds ~10-20 ns.
decisive_experiment: FPGA rig on commercial DDR4/DDR5 (~$80k): sweep tRCD and VARY per read to get per-cell margin as soft data, log error clustering per 512 b codeword, replay through soft LDPC versus BCH t=8.
prior_art: Phase B N-62; in-study I-11559 and I-11148 (ADVANCE, same family); Hi-ECC (ISCA 2010); NAND soft-sensing LDPC; static weak-cell erasure maps (US 8,898,544).

key_insight: Bond density works: each bitline needs one bond anywhere along its ~20 um length (~0.7 um2 per bond), so 0.5-0.8 um hybrid bonds can carry per-bitline sensing.
killer_doubt: One periphery cannot fit all physics: DRAM senses 14-60 mV of charge, MTJs ~10-50 uA at <0.5 V, PCM resets at ~100-200 uA, FeRAM pulses 1.5-3 V plates.
decisive_experiment: Programmable charge/current sense front-end chip at 130-180 nm, die-to-wafer bonded to MIM 1T1C and MTJ coupon arrays at a university hybrid-bond line (~$600k); compare margins with native test chips.
prior_art: YMTC Xtacking and Kioxia CBA bond arrays onto CMOS wafers; 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM plans with bonded periphery (training knowledge); foundry MPW test-chip programs.

key_insight: Selecting tiers by voltage instead of wiring would delete staircases and select lines; it works for ~4 tiers spaced ~0.5 V (5-7 decades apart), not 32.
killer_doubt: 32 levels in ~3 V sit ~90 mV apart; at SS 70 mV/dec adjacent tiers differ ~1.3 decades, so tier k+1 leaks during reads; any write rewrites all lower tiers.
decisive_experiment: 4-8 stacked IGZO TFTs on one gate with thickness-set Vt at a university fab (~$150k): measure per-tier Vt sigma and differential-read error versus level spacing at 85 C.
prior_art: NAND multi-level reads step wordline voltage to sort Vt levels; Vt-coded tier selection for 3D DRAM: none found.

key_insight: Vacuum is a wear-free, trap-free barrier: a 3 nm gap tunnels ~exp(-65) at rest, and Fowler-Nordheim gives ~1e12 on/off under V/3 biasing, a genuine crossbar selector.
killer_doubt: No gain stage: a 20x20 nm island over 4 nm vacuum is ~0.9 aF, ~5 e- at 1 V, ~90 uV on 10 fF. A sense transistor makes it N-09.
decisive_experiment: Sacrificial-release 5-10 nm W/Pt emitter gaps onto the floating gate of a reference MOSFET (~$250k): measure write-current spread, 85 C retention and drift after 1e10 pulses.
prior_art: Phase B N-09 nanogap floating node (ALIVE-SPEC); NASA Ames nanoscale vacuum-channel transistors (training knowledge); Spindt field-emitter arrays.

key_insight: Indium-free ZnSnO is a useful materials hedge for the vertical CCD family; one sense/restore node per string regenerates every packet each pass.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-08763, N-08 and imec's 3D IGZO CCD. a-Ga2O3 mobility is likely <1-5 cm2/Vs with deep traps; ~100 transfers per pass need CTE >=0.999.
decisive_experiment: Fold into the I-08763 test chip: add ZnSnO and a-Ga2O3 channel splits on the same planar CCD mask; compare CTE versus clock and 85 C hold. ~$50k extra.
prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar and IMW 2026 vertical 3D IGZO CCD; in-study I-10793 and I-01064 (ADVANCE); Phase B N-08.

key_insight: Charge shifts through a semiconductor channel, so wear is gate stress only (imec >1e10 cycles). A buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel keeps packets off interface traps, the main CTE loss.
killer_doubt: imec reports CTE >98% at ~4-6 MHz; ~120 transfers need >=0.999 each (89% survives). A 60-stage shift at 4 MHz takes 15 us, ~300x DRAM tRC.
decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 3-4 phase CCDs, surface versus buried IGO/IGZO heterochannel with fat-zero bias (~$300k): CTE versus clock 4-200 MHz at 25-125 C. Go if >=0.999 at >=50 MHz.
prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar and IMW 2026 vertical IGZO CCD; buried-channel oxide CCD: none found (via search snippet); in-study I-10793, I-01064.

key_insight: 3D NAND tools plus amplifier-per-string regeneration avoid EUV and per-bit contacts; streaming a whole string costs only ~0.2 pJ/bit of gate CV2 at 3 V.
killer_doubt: Overclaimed: a 150 nm hex hole is ~19,500 nm2, so 40 packets give ~490 nm2/bit before slits, not 250. 20 ns average needs ~3 GHz clocks; poly-Si traps cut CTE.
decisive_experiment: Covered by the I-08763 planar CCD chip: add a poly-Si channel split and a 120-transfer recirculating loop to measure cumulative loss and 85 C dark fill. ~$50k extra.
prior_art: Phase B N-08; imec IGZO CCD (IEDM 2024, IMW 2026); 1970s Fairchild and Intel CCD memories; in-study I-10793, I-05275.

key_insight: Circumferential magnetization round a vertical via is a closed-flux, stray-field-free bit; stacked planes as word straps would give 100+ tiers from one hole etch.
killer_doubt: Faraday read fails: 5 nm CoFeB over a 40 nm tier links ~3e-16 Wb, ~0.1 uV per 1 ns tilt; writes need ~0.7 mA per 50 nm pillar (3.5e7 A/cm2).
decisive_experiment: Drop inductive read: test TMR or AMR readout of circumferential domains in electroplated CoFeB/NiFe-lined 50-100 nm vias (~$200k), measuring switching current and thermal stability per tier.
prior_art: Plated-wire memory (UNIVAC, 1960s); in-study I-08865 (DROP, same numbers); Phase B N-82 racetrack in capacitor hole; Parkin racetrack.

key_insight: Trading stored bits for recomputed bits is sound where compute is cheap: a PRNG plus a few coefficients regenerates a weight block in a few cycles near memory.
killer_doubt: SeedLM-style seeds reach ~3-4 bits/weight, the same as production 4-bit quantization (GPTQ, MXFP4), so the gain over today's baseline is ~1-1.3x, not 3-8x.
decisive_experiment: Software only (~$20k GPU time): seed fitting versus GPTQ/AWQ at equal bits per weight on Llama-class models; report perplexity at 2-3 bits per weight.
prior_art: SeedLM (Apple, 2024 preprint; PRNG-seed weight compression, training knowledge); GPTQ, AWQ, MXFP4/NVFP4 formats; AQLM vector-quantization codebooks.

key_insight: The arithmetic holds (1.6 eV more gap cuts intrinsic generation ~3e13x), and 187 electrons on 0.1 fF sit far above the ~4 e- kTC floor.
killer_doubt: IGZO leakage is already defect- and gate-limited (<1 aA, 1e3-3e4 s retention), not intrinsic. a-Ga2O3 mobility <1-5 cm2/Vs slows writes; China supplies ~98% of gallium.
decisive_experiment: Side-by-side 2T0C cells, IGZO versus ALD a-Ga2O3 write device, on one BEOL run (~$150k): retention distributions over 1e4 cells at 85-125 C and write time at 1 V.
prior_art: IGZO 2T0C gain cells (imec, Kioxia OCTRAM); in-study I-03018 Ga2O3 coaxial cell (DROP); university Ga2O3 TFT work.

key_insight: For sub-32 B random words (graphs, sparse matrices) a base-die gather removes most wasted link bytes, and HBM4 custom logic base dies make it buildable.
killer_doubt: Named workloads are already dense: KV pages 2 KB+, embedding rows 128-512 B, MoE tokens KBs, against 32 B granules; gain under ~10% of AI traffic. Row overfetch untouched.
decisive_experiment: Trace study (~$30k): replay KV-cache, embedding and MoE address traces through a 32 B-sector HBM model and count PHY bytes saved by gather-pack versus controller sector coalescing.
prior_art: Impulse memory controller (Utah, 1999); GS-DRAM (MICRO 2015); RecNMP (ISCA 2020); in-study I-10911 (DROP); HBM4 custom base dies.

key_insight: One bit-plane-major copy serves several precisions, making precision a fetch-time knob; most useful for KV-score sketches and batch-1 edge decode.
killer_doubt: Production already stores 4-bit weights, and batched serving fetches the most planes any token needs, so dynamic savings fall to ~1.1-1.3x of decode traffic.
decisive_experiment: Software emulation (~$30k): bit-plane fetch policy on Llama-class decode at batch 1, 32 and 128; measure bytes moved and accuracy against a static 4-bit baseline.
prior_art: Any-Precision LLM (ICML 2024); Matryoshka Quantization (2025); Stripes bit-serial accelerator; in-study I-02063 (HOLD), I-05653 and I-09970 (DROP).
